title: The finite-subextension cocone is a colimit in condensed abelian groups
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $I$ be the poset of finite intermediate fields $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Qlb$, ordered by inclusion, as in [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Work in a universe containing $\Qlb$, so that $I$ is a small filtered category. Give $E$ the topology restricted from $\Qlb$ and write $\underline E(S)=C(S,E)$ for its condensed ring on profinite sets with the coherent topology [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Let $A=\underline{\Qlb}$ be the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]; thus
$$
A(S)=\{a\in C(S,\Qlb)\mid a(S)\subseteq E\text{ for some }E\in I\}.
$$
Consider the diagram $D:I\to\Sh(*_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Ab)$ with $D(E)$ the underlying abelian sheaf of $\underline E$ and transition $D(E\subseteq F)=\iota_{E,F}$ of [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map]. Its cocone with vertex the underlying abelian sheaf of $A$ and legs $j_E:\underline E\to A$ of [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-to-qlbar] is a colimit in $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Ab)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Explicitly, for any condensed abelian group $G$ and additive sheaf morphisms $a_E:\underline E\to G$ satisfying $a_F\circ\iota_{E,F}=a_E$ whenever $E\subseteq F$, there exists a unique additive sheaf morphism $a:A\to G$ satisfying $a\circ j_E=a_E$ for every $E\in I$.

source.place: Entire point-colimit proof; existing project declaration Profinite.isColimitPadicAlgClRingObjCocone, WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.RingObjects.Condensed.FiniteSubextension, lines 173–196

proof.text: By [det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed-subextensions](1), $I$ is nonempty and any two fields have a common finite overfield. It is small in the universe fixed in the statement, since its objects are subfields of the fixed set $\Qlb$ and its arrows are inclusions. By [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map], the transition maps satisfy the identity and composition laws, giving $D$. By [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-to-qlbar], $j_F\circ\iota_{E,F}=j_E$. Thus these actual sectionwise inclusions define the stated cocone of abelian sheaves on the site of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring].

source.place: Paragraph 1: diagram and cocone; paragraph 2: directed index

proof.text: For a profinite $S$, every $x\in A(S)$ takes values in some finite $E$, by [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Its corestriction $x_E:S\to E$ is continuous: if $U=E\cap V$ is open in the subspace topology, with $V$ open in $\Qlb$, then $x_E^{-1}(U)=x^{-1}(V)$ is open. Hence $x_E\in C(S,E)$ as in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and $j_{E,S}(x_E)=x$ by [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-to-qlbar]. Conversely each $j_{E,S}$ has values in $A(S)$ and is injective, since equality after inclusion into $\Qlb$ is pointwise equality in $E$. This identifies $A(S)$ with the union of these section groups inside $C(S,\Qlb)$.

source.place: Paragraphs 2–3: injectivity and identification of the union by continuous corestriction

proof.text: Fix a compatible cocone $a_E:\underline E\to G$. For $x\in A(S)$ choose a representation $x=j_{E,S}(x_E)$ from step 2 and put $a_S(x)=a_{E,S}(x_E)$. If also $x=j_{F,S}(x_F)$, choose a finite $H$ containing $E,F$ by [det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed-subextensions](1). The images of $x_E$ and $x_F$ in $C(S,H)$ under [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map] agree pointwise, since both have image $x$ in $\Qlb$. The compatibility $a_H\circ\iota_{E,H}=a_E$ and $a_H\circ\iota_{F,H}=a_F$ then gives $a_{E,S}(x_E)=a_{F,S}(x_F)$. Thus $a_S$ is independent of every choice.

source.place: Paragraph 2: universal property of the directed union, with representative independence written out

proof.text: For $x,y\in A(S)$ choose representatives over $E,F$ and a common finite $H$ using [det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed-subextensions](1). Write $x_H,y_H\in C(S,H)$ for their images. The pointwise operations of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] and [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] give $x+y=j_{H,S}(x_H+y_H)$. Independence in step 3 and additivity of $a_{H,S}$ therefore give $a_S(x+y)=a_{H,S}(x_H+y_H)=a_S(x)+a_S(y)$. The zero section is represented by the zero function over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, so $a_S(0)=0$. Consequently every $a_S$ is an abelian-group homomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph 2: the directed-union universal map is additive

proof.text: For a continuous map $u:T\to S$ of profinite sets, represent $x\in A(S)$ by $x_E\in C(S,E)$. The restrictions in [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] and [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] are precomposition, so $x|_T$ is represented by $x_E\circ u$ over the same $E$. Naturality of the given sheaf morphism $a_E$ yields $a_T(x|_T)=a_{E,T}(x_E\circ u)=G(u)(a_{E,S}(x_E))=G(u)(a_S(x))$. Thus the homomorphisms $a_S$ are a natural transformation of the underlying presheaves. Since $A$ and $G$ are sheaves, such a natural transformation is exactly an additive sheaf morphism $a:A\to G$.

source.place: Paragraph 3: the sectionwise union identification is natural, and the vertex is already a sheaf

proof.text: For $x_E\in C(S,E)$, the choice of its own representative gives $a_S(j_{E,S}(x_E))=a_{E,S}(x_E)$, so $a\circ j_E=a_E$, with the legs of [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-to-qlbar]. If $b:A\to G$ has the same composites, represent any $x\in A(S)$ by $j_{E,S}(x_E)$ as in step 2. Then $b_S(x)=b_S(j_{E,S}(x_E))=a_{E,S}(x_E)=a_S(x)$. Equality on all sections implies $b=a$. This proves existence and uniqueness for every compatible cocone, precisely the colimit universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Paragraph 3: conclude the colimit using its explicit universal property

proof_origin.place: The blueprint point-colimit proof, with its sectionwise directed-union argument expanded into the additive natural universal map; no general sheafification theorem is needed.

The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from side-live. The statement matches the raw blueprint proposition: the same index poset of finite subextensions, the subspace topology on each E, a vertex of finite-subextension-valued maps (not all of C(-,Qlb)), and the category Sh(*_proet,Ab). The 6 steps write out the source's sectionwise directed-union route. (1) det-subextensions(1) gives a nonempty directed index, and the definition nodes give the functor laws and j_F∘ι=j_E. (2) Corestriction is continuous and j_E is injective, so A(S) is the union of the C(S,E). (3) The value does not depend on the representative, by comparing in a common compositum H. (4) The map is additive, and zero is represented over Q_l. (5) It is natural under precomposition, and A and G are sheaves, so it is a morphism of sheaves. (6) Factorization and uniqueness follow, which is the colimit definition. Every step is correct and genuinely elementary from cited statements, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Proving the universal property directly removes the need for the generic sheafification-of-colimits fact; no argument of the source is dropped. Edge cases checked: S empty, S a point, a section represented over two fields, G=0, non-locally-constant maps; using all of C(-,Qlb) would break step 2, and the statement excludes it. There are no new nodes and no duplicate in the DAG; the closure (173 nodes) is acyclic; no SGA is used; the three Mathlib search kinds are recorded with real results. I accept the declared tool_uses (det-subextensions is on the route through sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed; the other two are definitions); none was actually needed.
